observations: Torah LM2 #21 is one of the shortest teachings in the corpus — two sentences, one principle, zero bechina equivalences. The text teaches that when one innovates Torah (חִדּוּשֵׁי תוֹרָה), hostile forces watch for an opportunity (אֵלּוּ הַיְדוּעִים, הַמִּסְתַּכְּלִים וּמְצַפִּים), and studying the Poskim before and after the chiddush creates a protective guard (אַנְשֵׁי חַיִל עִם כְּלֵי זַיִן). The sole concept cluster potentially present is: חידושי תורה / פוסקים / אנשי חיל / כלי זין — but these concepts are linked exclusively through eitza (cause-effect) flow, not through bechina (shared-nature) equations. The text does not state that any concept IS a bechina of another in the equivalence sense. The phrase 'נַעֲשִׂין בְּחִינַת אַנְשֵׁי חַיִל' describes the functional outcome of an action, not a structural identity between two concepts. No independent domain of 3+ concepts connected by explicit bechina language exists. The requirement for a new package proposal — 3+ concepts connected by explicit bechina language forming an independent domain — is not met. NO_NEW_PACKAGES.
